 *******
 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Abdul Shakeer @ Shakeer Ahamed, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 20.12.2024 the said Abdul Shakeer @ Shakeer Ahamed was riding the Suzuki Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-52-U-6731 on the left side of Kunigal (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 Bypass - Ambedkar Circle Main Road, while so proceeding at about 12.00 p.m reached at opposite to Nandikeshwara Hotel, Nelamangala,
Bengaluru District, at that time suddenly the rider of TVS XL Super Moped bearing No.KA-52-X-1306 came from Kunigal Bypass towards Nelamangala side, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against Motor Cycle of said Abdul Shakeer @ Shakeer Ahamed and caused the accident.

Due to which he fell down along with the Motor Cycle and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to V.P. Magnus hospital, Nelamangala, wherein after first aid treatment, for further management referred to Sparsh hospital, Yeshawanthapura, Bengaluru,
wherein even after better and expert treatment to save the life, he succumbed to fatal injuries and died on 21.12.2024 during the course of treatment.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, medical, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.

Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 65 years and was earning his livelihood as Driver and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m, with the said earnings the deceased was maintaining his family members, since he was the only earning member in (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 the family.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner's life has become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship, without any member in the family and has lost beloved and caretaker husband.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Motor Cycle and in this regard the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending Motor Cycle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- to the petitioner with cost and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

Rihana vs Narasimhamurthy K on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121592867/
2 04.

The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the deceased, dependency of the petitioner with the deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 deceased, treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued the policy for the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-52-U-6731 and that was covered at the material time subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the deceased was solely responsible for the accident, in fact the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was no way responsible for the accident and death and the rider of the offending Motor Cycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving licence, thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed: -
ISSUES
01. Whether petitioner proves that she is the LRs/dependent of deceased Sri.Abdul Shakeer @ Shakeer Ahamed S/o Pacha Saheb?

02. Whether petitioner proves that deceased Sri.Abdul Shakeer @ Shakeer Ahamed S/o Pacha Saheb was died on 20.12.2024 at about 12.00 noon, near on Kunigal bypass-, (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 Ambedkar Circle Main Road, opposite to Nandikeshwara Hotel, due to rash and negligent riding of TVS XL bearing registration No.KA-52-X-1306 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether respondent No.2 proves that rider of TVS XL not having valid license?
04. Whether respondent No.2 proves that due to negligence of the deceased vehicle accident took place.
Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation?
05. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
06 . What order or award?
06. In order to prove her case, the petitioner was got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed her side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

Rihana vs Narasimhamurthy K on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121592867/
3

09. My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.1272/2025  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : In the Negative  Issue No.4 : In the Negative  Issue No.5 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.6 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
Petitioner filed affidavit stated that, she is the wife of the deceased.

To prove the said fact, she has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of herself and deceased and Death certificate of the deceased as per Ex.P.15 to 17 which shows that the petitioner is wife of the deceased.
There is no dispute in her cross-examination regarding relationship of the petitioner with the deceased.
So on perusal of these documents, it is true that the petitioner is the legal representative and dependent on the deceased.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner got herself examined as PW.1 and she has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and she has reiterated the petition (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 averments therein.

In her cross-examination she has stated that she has not seen the accident and Motor Cycle was belongs to her son Mujamil Ahamed and she do not know whether her son was given reply stating that her husband was not having driving licence to ride the Motor Cycle and admits that accident occurred at U turn.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Nelamangala Traffic Police against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.2 and 3 are the Complaint and further Complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending Motor Cycle, the accident took place and injured sustained injuries and later he died during the course of treatment.

Ex.P.4 and 5 are Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident on Kunigal Circle - Ambedkar Circle Road, near Nandikeshwara Hotel, wherein the rider of offending Motor Cycle came from Kunigal Circle side towards Ambedkar Circle from West to East direction and dashed against the Motor Cycle of deceased while he was taking U turn towards South direction from Ambedkar Circle towards Kunigal Circle side, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is Inquest report of deceased Shakeer Ahamed.
Ex.P.7 is Post mortem report of deceased Shakeer Ahamed shows the (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 cause of death is due to hypovolenic shock due to road traffic accident.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.9 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending Motor Cycle has stated that one Bharath.V.R was riding the Motor Cycle and he had a valid driving licence and said Motor Cycle had valid insurance as on the date of accident.

Ex.P.10 is copy of IMV report Rihana vs Narasimhamurthy K on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121592867/
4 which discloses that both vehicles are involved in the accident and both vehicles are damaged at the front side.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex. P.11 is Statement of accused/rider of offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.12 is Wound certificate of accused/rider of offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.13 is Police intimation (02 in Nos.).

Ex.P.14 is Charge sheet shows that after completion of the investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against rider of the offending Motor Cycle for the offences punishable U/s 281,
125(b), 106 of BNS.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of offending Motor Cycle and deceased sustained injuries and later died during the course of treatment.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

12. Issues No.3 and 4:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
13.

The respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that the rider of TVS XL was not having valid licence and accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased vehicle who rode his Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner.

But in this regard the respondent No.2 did not examine any witnesses nor produced any documents and also in Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has clearly stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending Motor Cycle which clearly goes to show that the negligence is on the part of rider of the offending Motor Cycle itself and further in Charge sheet has not quoted any sections regarding non-possessing of driving licence by the rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Accordingly, Issues No.3 and 4 are answered in the negative.
14. Issue No.5:-

This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 death of the deceased Abdul Shakeer @ Shakeer Ahamed, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner has stated in her petition and chief-examination that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 65 years and was Driver by profession and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization, medical, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.

Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner's life has become dark,
miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
15. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioner has not produced any birth certificate, school records of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P.15.

Even though the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 14.12.1960.

The alleged accident occurred on 20.12.2024 and hence it appears Rihana vs Narasimhamurthy K on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121592867/
5 that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 64 years.
Therefore, (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 64 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 61 to 65 years is "7".

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioner has not produced any evidence or documents.

Hence, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding avocation and income, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2024 the notional income is Rs.16,500/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.16,500/-
p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner is the wife of the deceased and she is the dependent on the earnings of the deceased.
As the deceased was aged more than 60 years, the petitioner is not entitled for future prospects or additional income.

It is also evident that in the present case the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 petitioner is the only one dependent and hence 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (16,500 - 8,250) = Rs.8,250/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.8,250/-.
As the deceased was aged about 64 years, the multiplier of 7 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.6,93,000/- (Rs.8,250 x 12 x 7) towards loss of dependency.

18. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
19. The claimant is the wife of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioner would be entitled for Rs.48,400/-
towards loss of filial consortium and petitioner is entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi &
others case has calculated compensation as under;
 Sl. Head of Amount in  No. Compensation Rs.
 1. Loss of Dependency 6,93,000-00  (After deducting 50% of  the income towards  personal and living  expenses)
 2. Loss of filial consortium 48,400-00 Rihana vs Narasimhamurthy K on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121592867/
6  (For petitioner)

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 . Loss of estate 18,150-00  4. Funeral expenses and 18,150-00
transportation of dead  body

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,77,700/- with (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

21. Regarding liability:- To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.2 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has deposed that the Spot Sketch and Panchanama report would clearly shows that the deceased/rider was solely negligent in causing the accident and deceased himself hit the TVS XL and he was solely negligent in causing the accident
, as such the petition was not maintainable for one's own negligence.

In her cross-examination she admits that she was deposed based on the Police records and denied to the suggestion that the Police have filed Charge sheet against rider of TVS XL and she has produced 4 documents such as Ex.R.1 is Authorization letter.
Ex.R.2 is Policy which shows that the policy of the offending Motor Cycle was in force as on the date of accident.
Ex.R.3 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the deceased Motor Cycle.

Ex.R.4 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the deceased Motor Cycle has stated that one Shakeer Ahamed i.e., deceased was riding his Motor Cycle and said Motor Cycle had valid insurance (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 as on the date of accident and deceased rider was not having valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
Even if the deceased did not have a driving license at the time of the accident, the accident should not be considered to have been caused by his fault.
Respondent No.2 counsel argued to consider the contributory negligence as deceased was not having valid licence.
His prayer is untenable because Police documents clearly goes to show that Police have filed Charge sheet against the rider of offending Motor Cycle and there is no case against the deceased.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the R.C Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit above said compensation amount of Rs.7,77,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.5 partly in affirmative.

In view of reasons assigned to above Issues No.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly Rihana vs Narasimhamurthy K on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121592867/
7 allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,77,700/- (Rupees Seven lakhs seventy seven thousand and seven hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner being the wife of the deceased, on deposit of the compensation amount with interest, she is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30%
shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

(SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.1272/2025 Draw award accordingly.
